posts.text:
Poland has been erased from the map entirely — and rebuilt from scratch — more than once.

Four snapshots, one country, a thousand years of borders sliding across Europe — a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ Year 1000: Bolesław I the Brave hosts Emperor Otto III at the Congress of Gniezno. His Poland already stretches from the Baltic toward the Carpathians — one of the largest states in the region.

2/ 1596: the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, formed by the 1569 Union of Lublin, is one of the biggest states in Europe. That year King Sigismund III Vasa moves the capital from Kraków to Warsaw — where it remains today.
3/ By 1795, the Commonwealth is gone completely — partitioned to nothing by Russia, Prussia and Austria. Poland won't exist as a state again for 123 years.
4/ 1939: the Second Polish Republic, reborn in 1918 with borders confirmed after the Polish-Soviet War, is invaded from the west by Germany and from the east by the USSR within weeks of each other.
5/ 1945: the borders shift bodily westward. Poland loses its eastern territories to the Soviet Union along the Curzon Line, and gains former German land up to the Oder-Neisse line instead.
6/ Same nation, four completely different shapes on the map, one thousand years apart. Which historical border shift should we map next? Follow @forummapping and let us know.
